picks.brief: CEO Dara Khosrowshahi purchased 141,000 UBER shares (~$10.0M) on Sept 10-11, 2026, one of his largest open-market buys on record, and the stock rallied 2.1% to $72.56 on the news. The purchase came after UBER had fallen roughly 30% from its 52-week high and while the stock trades below both its 50-day ($73.67) and 200-day ($75.67) moving averages, making it a notable vote of confidence from management at depressed levels.
picks.bull_case: A CEO buying $10M of stock with his own money, especially after a steep drawdown, is a strong insider-confidence signal; management typically has the best visibility into near-term business trends and would be reluctant to buy heavily into a genuine deterioration.
picks.bear_case: A single insider buy, even a large one, doesn't offset the stock's broader downtrend (below both major moving averages, RSI a soft 39) or offer any new operational information; insider buys can also be poorly timed and are not a guarantee of a bottom.

picks.brief: A California court ordered Uber to pay $40 million in damages to the parents of a 23-year-old passenger who died after being left roadside by an Uber driver (ruling reported Sept 18, 2026). This adds to an existing pattern of rideshare safety litigation against Uber, including a separate federal jury assault verdict earlier in 2026 and a reported 3,000+ pending claims in related multidistrict litigation.
picks.bull_case: A single $40M judgment is immaterial against Uber's balance sheet and is likely appealable; litigation reserves and insurance may absorb much of the cost, and the market has shown limited reaction to prior similar rulings.
picks.bear_case: This is one data point in a growing, structural pattern of safety-related litigation exposure that could compound into meaningful legal costs, reputational damage, or regulatory scrutiny of the rideshare model over time.
